Hi Samantha — quick technical clarifications to support Laura's draft:

- Data classification: Redwood treats prompt inputs, generated outputs, and user identifiers as "customer-controlled data". We do not collect or retain customer prompts for model improvement unless the customer opts in explicitly.
- Processing locations: Control plane processes (account management, billing) are primarily in the US (GCP us-central/US regions); model serving for EU customers can be pinned to EU regions (we support us-west/eu-west/asia regions).
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed keys available via KMS integration (Bring-Your-Own-Key).
- KV/prefix caching: Some runtime caching occurs on serving nodes; cached values are ephemeral and purged per-configured TTL.
- Audit logs: Admin + token-level request logs retained 90 days by default; extended retention packages available.

I've uploaded a working folder with: redwood_dataflow_map_v3.pdf, subprocessor_register_export.csv, and a short ops note. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdEfgAuroraEvidence

Samantha / Daniel — attached is the compiled evidence pack and a short cover memo addressing the three specific asks Daniel raised. Highlights:

- Backups: Statement included — backups containing customer PII are encrypted and restoration across regions only occurs with explicit customer authorization or in case of DR declared by the customer’s account administrator.
